function.name: get_events
function.description: Returns events that have already happened, from oldest to newest. It never returns events later than the current time. Use it to see specific data (positions, wind, link, detections, your own alerts or operator messages). Choose the window by what the question gives: no time at all (the last one, the last three, the most recent; for the one before the last, ask for 2 and take the first) -> last_n; a moment or an interval with clock times -> since and until; an interval counted back from now (the last minute, the last 90 seconds) -> last_s. Use source all only when it is not clear which source the question is about or when the general state of the exercise is asked; if the question is about one source, give that source.

source.description: all = the events of every source together, ordered by time, each with its source (a few per source, and it says so if there are more); gps = PositionUpdated of the drone; radar = TrackUpdated of the ground radar; meteo = WindReported; link = LinkStatus of the command link; battery = BatteryStatus; mission = mission events; detector = rule-based detections; monitor = alerts published by the monitor; operator = operator messages. Without source it is all

type.description: Optional: filter by event type, e.g. WindReported

last_n.description: How many events (the most recent); with source all, how many of each source. Default 10 (3 with all), maximum 50

since.description: Optional: start of the window, in seconds or as a clock time (T+03:42, 03:42, T+1:02:03); the conversion is done for you. A start later than the current time is rejected

until.description: Optional: end of the window, in seconds or as a clock time (clipped to the current time, and it says so)

last_s.description: Optional: the last N seconds up to now (60, 90s, 1:30, 1m30s). Do not combine it with since

function.name: get_mission_plan
function.description: Returns the flight plan: waypoints with x,y coordinates in metres (x east, y north), cruise speed, estimated passing time and next pending waypoint.

function.name: get_track_metrics
function.description: Computes trajectory metrics over a window (since and until, or last_s for the last seconds up to now) from the GPS and the radar: deviation of each source from the planned route, distance between GPS and radar, drift direction, course of travel versus the bearing to the next waypoint, mean speed and the wind of the same window (mean speed, maximum gust, where it pushes and difference with the drift). It also returns the ids of the events used, to cite them as evidence, and a `now` block with how things are right now (last 10 seconds): the fix of the GPS, current GPS–radar distance and whether they agree, current deviation of the GPS and of the radar, the current wind already interpreted (where it comes from and where it pushes). When the GPS has no fix its position is only an estimate: the current GPS–radar distance, whether they agree and the current GPS deviation are then null.

since.description: start of the window, in seconds or as a clock time (T+03:42, 03:42, T+1:02:03); the conversion is done for you. A start later than the current time is rejected

until.description: end of the window, in seconds or as a clock time (clipped to the current time, and it says so)

last_s.description: alternative to since and until: the last N seconds up to now (60, 90s, 1:30, 1m30s)

function.name: get_my_alerts
function.description: Returns the alerts published by the monitor agent, with their status (open, closed or superseded).

only_open.description: true to see only the open ones. Default false

function.name: get_flight_summary
function.description: Summary of the whole flight: duration, distance according to GPS and to radar, waypoints reached, whether the mission was completed, detections per rule and alerts per cause.

function.name: publish_alert
function.description: Publishes an anomaly alert (AnomalyDetected event) with your diagnosis on the bus. It is your only way to act. If the data does not meet the format, it returns the errors so you can fix them.

detection_ids.description: Ids of the detections that motivate the alert (det-…). Optional if there is only one pending detection: the module fills it in

checks.description: Checks you made before choosing the cause; they are checked against the results of the tools. Fill them in BEFORE choosing cause

gps_alert_recent.description: The "Recent GPS alert" line of the state says yes

gps_radar_disagreed.description: gps_radar.disagreed from get_track_metrics (false if you did not call it)

wind_notable.description: wind.notable from get_track_metrics (false if there is no wind or you did not call it)

wind_with_drift.description: wind.with_drift from get_track_metrics (false if there is no wind or you did not call it)

link_checked.description: You called get_events with source link

link_anomalous.description: The link is anomalous (another controller_id, RSSI jump of more than 10 dB or much higher latency); null if you did not look at it

phase.description: Decide it before writing the texts, which must agree with it: `recovering` when the problem of the episode is over and the situation is going back to normal; `active` while the problem continues

confidence.description: Confidence in the cause, from 0 to 1

evidence_event_ids.description: 2 to 6 ids of events you have seen in the tools (e.g. met-0010, gps-000106) that support the diagnosis; they go here, not in the explanation

explanation.description: Reasoning with concrete data and times (T+mm:ss)

recommendation.description: What you recommend to the person in charge of the drone. Recommend only: you cannot act

supersedes.description: Optional: alert_id of an earlier alert of yours that this one replaces

function.name: acknowledge_detection
function.description: Responds to one or several detections without creating a new alert (publishes a DetectionAcknowledged event). Use it when the detection belongs to an alert of yours that is already open and neither its cause, its severity nor its phase changes (pass alert_id), or when you decide no alert is needed (do not pass alert_id).

detection_ids.description: Ids of the detections you respond to (det-…); they must be among those you were given. Optional if there is only one pending detection: the module fills it in

alert_id.description: Optional: alert_id of the open alert they belong to. If no alert is needed, do not pass it. On a closing warning for an alert, the module fills it in

function.name: close_alert
function.description: Closes an alert of yours that no longer applies (publishes an AlertClosed event; alerts are not modified).

alert_id.description: The alert you close. Optional on a closing warning: the module fills in that warning's alert

reason.description: Why it is closed, with data

function.name: load_skill
function.description: Loads a skill (diagnosis or format procedure) from those listed in the index of the system prompt and returns its content.

name.description: Exact name of the skill, e.g. route-deviation
